newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas still mixed late, cash holds.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas still mixed late, cash holds.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were still narrowly mixed late Thursday, but trade remained light and prices held recent technical ranges amid little conviction about market direction, industry sources said.
At 1405 EST, December was down by 1.9 cents at $2.665 per million British thermal units, while January was 0.8 cent lower at $2.67. Other deferreds were narrowly mixed.

"I like where we are now. When we get (cold) weather, we should move into the $2.70s (basis December), and when we don't, we'll test the $2.50s," said one Houston-based trader, noting cash held relatively steady today.

With near-term weather forecasts looking supportive and winter still ahead, few expected prices to collapse anytime soon, but traders noted significant open interest in December that could soon pressure the spot contract as longs liquidate before the November 21 expiration.
Revised 6-10 day forecasts call for below-normal weather in the eastern third of the nation, while the western two-thirds are expected to stay mostly above-normal.
Technically, traders said recent ranges were intact, with December support still pegged at $2.52-2.53 and resistance at $2.745 and then at the $2.88 contract high.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices were unchanged Thursday at about $2.70. Midwest prices were steady to up slightly at about $2.60. Forecasts for cold weather this weekend kept New York city gate gas prices in the mid-$2.90s.
NYMEX said 17,948 Hub contracts traded at 1335 EST.
NYMEX December Alberta natgas firmed 1.5 cents to a new contract high of $1.27, while most other months were untraded at 1400 EST. NYMEX said 20 Alberta contracts traded at 1335 EST.
NYMEX Permian natgas was untraded at 1400 EST but December was offered unchanged at $2.51.
On the KCBT, December slipped three cents to $2.49, while Januray was two cents lower at $2.50. The December East/West spread widened by 1.1 cents to 17.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
